items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: As Toprak’s designated successor, Nicolò lived up to expectations, bringing Italy back to the top of Superbike, 14 years after Biaggi. This marks the culmination of a journey that will lead him to reunite with Rossi and return to where it all began.

items.title: Toprak Razgatlioglu reveals when he thought to “stop racing”
items.excerpt: Toprak Razgatlioglu says his difficult MotoGP rookie season reminds him of 2018, when he even considered stopping racing.

items.title: Petrucci: “I’m sad because I’m saying goodbye to Superbike in the worst possible way”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I don’t know which way to go with this bike anymore. I knew that by coming here I could either win or quit, but a year ago I would have bet a hundred times on BMW: I’m where I’ve wanted to be for two years.”

items.title: How Alvaro Bautista is trying to generate “more options” for 2027 race seat
items.excerpt: WorldSBK champion Alvaro Bautista says his performance at the end of 2026 will be key to his chances of finding a good race seat for 2027.

items.title: Lecuona: "No one has Dall'Igna's mindset; this victory—and more—is proof of that"
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: "The secret is to always listen to everyone—a mindset that’s different from the Japanese. It took me a year to build up this confidence on the Ducati. I didn’t think I’d win by 5 seconds."

items.title: Nicolo Bulega vows to maintain WorldSBK “approach” despite “big” MotoGP test crash
items.excerpt: Nicolo Bulega says he will not change his “approach” to the Italian WorldSBK weekend despite his title chance and a recent test crash.

items.title: Surra: “I screwed up, but Acosta and Marquez also make mistakes”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I’d never been up at the front like that before; I had everything under control, and maybe that’s why I made a mistake. It’s all part of the process. Pole position? I thought I could do it, but Lecuona and Bulega are better prepared than I am.”

items.title: Bulega: “I’m not completely comfortable on the Ducati: I’m riding at 90%”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “Sometimes you have to be smart and avoid doing stupid things. I didn’t think Iker had that much leeway. We’ll see tomorrow, though.”

items.title: Toprak: "This year reminds me of my first year in SBK, when I thought about quitting."
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: "For me, it's even tougher now than it was in 2018, because I've won three titles—I'm used to winning. Back then, finishing 12th was bad, but not as bad as it is now. The Michelins? I just can't get the softs to work."

items.title: Luzzi: “Márquez has Stoner’s talent and Lorenzo’s determination”
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: The engineer, who has worked with all three, describes the qualities that make them champions: Jorge’s determination, Casey’s raw talent and Marc’s ability to combine both.

items.title: THE BOOK Johann Zarco, victory and forgiveness
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: Written in collaboration with Michel Turco, it is the result of 10 hours of interviews. There could be a sequel.

items.title: Lecuona: “For the first time, I can say that I’m really enjoying riding the Ducati”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “I rode in my own style; I’m consistent and had a little margin to work with. Bulega’s stats? I looked at them—he always does something better than I do. I feel stronger than I did at Donington, so why not aim for the win?”

items.title: Surra: "The V4-S and the Superbike? The only thing they have in common is the Ducati name—everything else is different."
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: "The two bikes are totally different. I'm feeling confident about tomorrow, but I'm not saying anything. Today, my crew chief worked some magic on the bike."

items.title: Bulega: “The crashes? It’s strange what happened today on the Ducati”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “The Panigale was bouncing around, but maybe we've figured out why. The title celebration? I don’t want to know anything about it: they can even dress me up as Spider-Man or Superman.”

items.title: Dixon: “I’m not going through hell for nothing—this MotoGP burns young riders out”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “Riders start so early that by the time they’re 30, they’re already burned out. My wife’s illness has given me motivation and makes me believe that one day we’ll be champions. Redding? You have to build your own path.”

items.title: Zambenedetti: “The new regulation will be drastic and will eliminate Ducati’s advantage”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: INTERVIEW - “The engine will be completely different, and we’ll face more challenges, but we’re working on it. If Superbike turns the tables, we have to ask ourselves if it’s still the right championship for Ducati.”

items.title: Pirro: “Bulega the favorite in the MotoGP? It’s just pre-race tactics. Testing isn’t the same as racing.”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “It’s too early to judge. We’ll see how things stand once we have some solid data. Ducati was expected to struggle at Misano but dominated. At Spielberg, it was expected to win easily but struggled. There’s no logic to it. We’re taking it one day at a time.”

items.title: Bulega: “Pol Espargarò? There’s not much to say really—it’s not true that the Ducati 850 is made for me.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “There’s no rule that prevents a Superbike rider from testing a MotoGP bike. DAZN? If I want to say something that won’t be heard, I won’t say it in front of a camera.”

items.title: Lecuona: “Next year will be completely different on the Ducati”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: “Michelin tyres perform differently than Pirellis, so the bike handles differently and needs to be ridden differently. I’ve tried every chance I’ve had to beat Bulega, and I’ll do the same here at Cremona.”

items.title: Bassani: “Bulega’s Lamborghini? I had to pay for my car”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “Nicolò deserves that car; if they don’t give it to him, who should they give it to? Ducati has done an incredible job this year. The 2027 Bimota is a little different.”

items.title: Petrucci: “Racing in the Superbike doesn’t make sense anymore if they ask you for money”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “The MotoAmerica BMW is nothing like the Ducati from four years ago. BMW asked me to race and be a test rider. I’ll make a decision this weekend.”

items.title: Quadranti: “MV Agusta? It’s like fighting windmills. The future of Arenas isn’t up to me.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: INTERVIEW – “I chased the title with MV Agusta for ten years. Returning to Superbike with Arenas? It’s something to consider: I know Albert wants to race in SBK, but his future isn’t in my hands.”

items.title: Filippo Bianchi racing in 2027 Sportbike World Championship with Prodina XCI Racing
items.author: GPOne
items.excerpt: The 21-year-old from Tuscany will joining as the Italian champion in his class, making his debut on a Kawasaki Ninja ZX-6R 636: “It’s the fulfillment of a dream I’ve had since I was a child.”

items.title: Torres: “I was in danger of not racing this year; this is the beginning of a great story”
items.author: Daniela Piazza
items.excerpt: The new V2 Future Champ winner speaks out: “I don’t come from a wealthy family; we don’t have 200,000 euros to spend. If Pirro hadn’t offered me a test, I would have kept working. The secret to the Spaniards’ success? Their mindset.”

items.title: Marc Marquez: "Acosta is the rider who can beat me"
items.author: Gianluigi Mazza
items.excerpt: "He's the right rider. Pedro will be one of the big names next year and in the future. He can learn a lot about how to ride the Ducati. I'm Marc, and I'll give it my all."

items.title: Iannone: “Granado? Just a racing incident. The telemetry shows I did everything the same way.”
items.author: Riccardo Guglielmetti
items.excerpt: “Granado didn’t want my apology, and I understand that. I’ve never kicked anyone out in my career. The future? I don’t know—the day before Austin, my bags were packed, but I didn’t leave.”
